deities: Shri Sai Baba of Shirdi (19th-20th century saint; samadhi and marble statue)
festivals: Vijayadashami (Sai Baba's Punyatithi / Mahasamadhi day - temple open overnight)

history.period: Built as Buti Wada circa 1918; Baba's Mahasamadhi on 15 October 1918
history.summary: The Samadhi Mandir is the heart of Shirdi, housing the mortal remains (samadhi) of Sai Baba, the saint who arrived in Shirdi in the mid-19th century and lived there until his Mahasamadhi in 1918. The stone building was constructed by the wealthy devotee Gopalrao Buti as a wada (mansion) intended for Lord Krishna, but Baba himself was laid to rest there. Behind the white-marble samadhi stands a life-size idol of Sai Baba in Italian marble. The Shri Saibaba Sansthan Trust manages the temple, which follows a rigid daily schedule of four aartis (Kakad, Madhyana, Dhoop, Shej) maintained for decades, and runs one of India's largest free-food kitchens (Prasadalaya). The shrine is a major symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity - the complex also includes Dwarkamai, the mosque where Baba lived for 60 years, with its ever-burning Dhuni whose sacred ash (Udi) is distributed to devotees.

name: Shri Sai Baba Samadhi Mandir
town_description: Shirdi is a pilgrimage town in Rahata taluka of Ahmednagar district, Maharashtra, about 83 km from Ahmednagar and 307 km from Mumbai. Built around the life and samadhi of Sai Baba, it is one of India's busiest pilgrimage centres, attracting tens of millions of devotees of all faiths every year. The town is served by its own international airport and the Sainagar Shirdi railway station.

travel.road: 83 km from Ahmednagar, 307 km from Mumbai, 112 km from Nashik and 126 km from Aurangabad by well-maintained highways.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (verify); Thursdays are the most crowded. Phones and cameras cannot be carried inside the main temple area.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): reported as 4:00 AM-11:00 PM and 5:00 AM-10:00 PM. Four aartis: Kakad 4:30 AM, Madhyana 12:00 PM, Dhoop at sunset, Shej 10:30 PM; open overnight on Guru Purnima, Dussehra and Ram Navami.
